title: Telemetry-driven Remediation Orchestrator
creator: Lena Morales
description: Build a lightweight orchestrator that converts operational telemetry signals (alerts, anomaly scores, regression detections) into safe, idempotent remediation task graphs executed by our runbook-runner. The orchestrator will: 1) subscribe to telemetry sources (Prometheus alerts, Sentry anomalies, Redwood Console regression alerts); 2) map signals to curated remediation playbooks expressed as small tasklets; 3) perform a preflight simulation/dry-run against a shadow evaluator; 4) escalate to human operator with suggested next steps if confidence < threshold; 5) when gated, trigger automated remediation with audit logging and automatic rollback hooks. This reduces mean time to repair for common operational classes (cache poisoning, KV-cache exhaustion, model OOMs, routing failures) while preserving safety and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingest adapters implemented for Prometheus alertmanager and Console regression alerts
Remediation playbook registry with at least 5 curated playbooks (cache_clear, node_recycle, route_fallback, rate_limit_increase, kv_cache_truncate)
Dry-run simulator validates playbook idempotency and surfaces a deterministic list of side-effects
Operator approval flow in Console with single-click approve/reject and detailed audit trail
Automated rollback hooks that restore previous routing or config within SLA on failure
End-to-end test harness demonstrating a simulated KV-cache exhaustion alert => safe automated remediation in staging
Documentation and runbook for SREs: design, failure modes, failure recovery steps, and escalation matrix
notes: Initial spike showed telemetry->playbook mapping accuracy at ~82% for historical incidents (sampled 30 incidents). We need a confidence scoring step to avoid false positives.

Trade-off: full automation vs human-in-loop. Default policy will be human-ack for high-impact playbooks (cluster recycle, model restart) and auto for low-impact ops (route fallback, token bucket increase).

Security considerations: all remediation actions must be executed by a service account with restricted scopes and recorded in audit logs. KMS keys for any secrets will be fetched via short-lived tokens.
We will reuse runbook DSL from runbook-runner v2.1 but build a thin translation layer that compiles curated playbooks into the runner's typed tasklets.
Edge-case: playbook simulation must detect cascading side-effects (e.g., node recycle causing cold-start latency spike). Simulator will annotate estimated latency uplift and surface to approver.
